The HTML file is not a document that opens an app: it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up: about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) is ideal.
  2. Double-click PaycheckBudgetPlanner.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. A few short slides on your paycheck, bills, spending money and backups.
  4. Follow the three steps on This paycheck: add your paycheck, your bills, and your spending and saving. The usual bills and spending are one click away.
  5. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore sample data on the welcome screen or in Settings & backup. A fictional household with two incomes, 12 bills and a spending plan fills every screen, in a separate session. Return to my paychecks brings back your own, untouched.

The idea

One paycheck at a time.

You’re paid every week, two weeks or twice a month, and bills don’t wait for the end of the month. So the planner budgets each paycheck on its own.

This paycheck. The big number is what’s left after its bills, spending and saving; the ring shows where it goes.

WordWhat it means
This paycheckFrom your payday to the day before your next one.
Left overThe paycheck − its bills − spending − saving.
ShortIts bills and plans add up to more than it brings in.
Main paycheckThe income “each paycheck” amounts follow, when there are two.

Your paydays

Add your paycheck.

Paydays → Add an income, or the first setup step. Add a partner’s or side job’s pay the same way.

FieldWhat to enter
Take-home payWhat lands in your account, after tax. $2,150 or 1980.50 are fine.
How oftenEvery week, every 2 weeks, twice a month or once a month.
Next paydayFor weekly and every 2 weeks: check your last pay stub. Every later payday follows from it.
Paid onFor twice a month: the two days, like the 15th and the last day.
On a weekendPaid the Friday before, the Monday after, or that day.

Did your paycheck arrive?

On payday, This paycheck asks. Confirm amount with what actually came in: overtime, fewer hours, a bonus. The plan uses the real number.

Two incomes

Every payday from either one starts a paycheck. “Each paycheck” spending follows your main paycheck; change it with Make main.

Each payday

Bills and spending money.

Each bill lands in the paycheck before it’s due. Tick it off as you pay it, and log what you spend.

Spending & saving

Groceries, gas, fun money, savings: an amount each paycheck, or each month split by the days each paycheck covers.

Plan ahead

See a short paycheck coming.

Paycheck plan shows the next 6 or 12 paychecks side by side, and what each one leaves.

A red barThat paycheck is short: its bills and plans are more than it brings in.
⇄ on a billPay it from another paycheck, usually an earlier one with room. It stays there until you move it back.
Carry what’s leftEach paycheck starts with what the one before left (or owes).

Looking back

How every paycheck went.

Past paychecks: what came in, went to bills, was spent and saved, and what was left at the end.

“Ended with” uses what you actually spent, not what you planned, so it tells you which paychecks really ran short. Export it all as CSV.

50/30/20, 70/20/10, 80/20 or zero-based

This paycheck compares how it’s split with a budget method. Switch methods on the card or in Settings. Open Is each line a need, a want, saving or debt? to fix any line the app guessed wrong.

Keeping your paychecks safe.

Everything lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy, including us.

Your entries live in browser storage: please read

  • Everything you enter or import is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers: data added in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your data.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup: every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every paycheck, bill, payment, spending entry and category. Restore backup brings it back on any computer. The app reminds you when a backup is due.

Daily folder backup: Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this; use Download backup instead.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appExtract the ZIP first, then right-click the file → Open with → your browser.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
A bill is in the wrong paycheckIt goes in the paycheck its due date falls in. Check the bill’s next due date, or use ⇄ to move it.
A paycheck looks too shortTwo incomes? Make sure the right one is the main paycheck on Paydays.
Spending money looks smallA month amount is split by days: a short paycheck (a day or two) gets a small share.
My payday movedEdit the income and set the next payday; every later one follows.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Currency, or type your own symbol. Amounts are not converted.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Welcome tour → Show tour.
